newsitem.title: CHINA: China denies report of troops in Zaire.
newsitem.headline: China denies report of troops in Zaire.

text.p: China on Tuesday dismissed as groundless reports by Zairean rebels that 400 Chinese troops had flown into the capital, Kinshasa, to bolster the embattled government of President Mobutu Sese Seko.
"Recently some people issued rumours that China had sent troops to join Zaire's civil war and to provide arms to Zaire," a Foreign Ministry spokesman said.
"These reports are groundless," the spokesman said. "These are attempts to sow discord in the friendly relations between China and Zaire."

A top official of Laurent Kabila's rebel movement, Mwana Nanga Mawanpanga, read a statement on Monday from Kabila in which he said the alliance had "learned of the arrival of large contingents of Chinese troops in Kinshasa. We know of 400 troops at present."
He had "no clue" where the Chinese troops had come from, Mawanpanga told a news conference in Lubumbashi, Zaire's rebel-held second city.
"If the Chinese government did not send these troops, they can respond by a declaration. If they do not -- they may have been sent by the Chinese government," he said.
China said it wanted to see peace in Zaire, supported peace efforts by other African countries and the United Nations and opposed the presence of any foreign troops in Zaire's civil war.

"China has always believed that the issue of Zaire should be resolved by the people of Zaire and opposes the interference of foreign forces in Zaire's internal affairs," the Foreign Ministry spokesman said.
Zaire's government vowed on Monday its beleaguered army would never surrender the capital, Kinshasa, to advancing rebels and called on residents to be prepared for resistance.
Rebels have seized half of Zaire's vast territory since taking up arms in October to topple President Mobutu. Kinshasa is the most important city still in government hands.

South Africa is leading a diplomatic initiative backed by the United Nations and Washington to bring Mobutu and Kabila together to negotiate an end to the conflict, but finding an acceptable venue is the latest stumbling block.
